articles.title: Where AI Meets Instinct in Formula 1
GTA VI is More Than Just a Violent Crime Thriller. It's an Unexpected Exercise in Love and Empathy
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI is inescapable; everyone is talking about it. Even people and venues you wouldn’t expect are taking notice. I certainly didn’t have The Weather Channel and Anderson Cooper on my bingo card. Workers are taking time off to play and teachers have alternately canceled classes and bribed their students not to play hooky. articles.title: Havana, Caracas and Trump’s Unfinished Business in Latin America
articles.summary: “I want to get Cuba done before I leave you,” President Donald Trump told a conservative radio host on Nov. 12. It is a reminder that, despite the historic beating his party took in the midterm elections, Trump continues to see Latin America as a crucial part of his legacy. articles.title: Immigration Is Not a Fringe Issue
articles.summary: At a Senate forum on ICE violence, I listened to the sons of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo describe the morning their father was shot dead by ICE agents while on his way to work. Besides them sat and wept the families of Renee Nicole Good and Alex Pretti . Next to me were clergy wearing t-shirts that said “ Connected Americans ” and whispering prayers as they listened to the testimony of families whose loved ones had been killed in the streets. articles.title: Measles Is Back in the U.S. What Happens Next?
articles.summary: On Nov. 17, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) declared that measles is no longer considered "eliminated" in the U.S. In the past year, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recorded more than 5,800 cases of measles—the highest caseload since 1991. Vaccination programs and increased monitoring of incoming measles cases helped the U.S. to eliminate measles in 2000, meaning there was no consistent spread of the virus within the country for more than a year.
